industry.why: Double Underweight, carried unchanged, with the counter-case strengthened and named. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): property is valued off a yield and financed with leverage, the US 10-year is near 5.10%, the Fed hikes in December, and real estate was not spoken to as an industry. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: F now, D prior at industry level, every property sector D or F. The counter-case is stronger this week than at any time since the row was set: yields fell on firm data, Goldman Sachs upgraded bonds to overweight 'moving from headwind to hedge' (16 and 19 Oct), and real estate investment trusts were among the only sectors bought (Jefferies desk, 17 Oct); if that rally is a trend, this is the row where the tilt costs most, and it is the first row I would lift. Held at F because one week's rally with the policy rate still rising is a hedge working, not a peak, and the condition on the sector rows (back to D if the US 10-year falls under 4.5%) is 60 basis points away.

memo.verdict: PARK. Medium-high conviction. Do not progress Castellum to Early-Stage Assessment on current evidence; keep the case file open on a quarterly monitoring cadence rather than the annual re-screen. The memo reaches park because three of the four investment pillars fail (thematic fit, case simplicity, value-chain dynamics all grade D) while change forces alone reach C, and because the entry point is the worst in the twelve-month window: the shares sit 17.2% above their 200-day average and roughly 15% above the SEK 115 median consensus target of the three named brokers. The park is not a kill. Element E8 Required Attribute RA3 grades A, top decile of the named peer set, and a case carrying a top-decile corporate-change score is worth monitoring rather than discarding. Five named reassessment triggers, not a calendar date:
case: The case for park runs in five steps, in the memo's own order.

Step one: the change forces are genuine and unusually dense, so the name deserves a file. Seven distinct corporate change events landed inside twelve months: an activist stake at 25.4%, an extraordinary general meeting, a board replacement, a chair change, a chief executive change, a chief financial officer change and a strategy replacement. Element E8 Required Attribute RA3 walks the framework's nine corporate-change deltas and finds seven firing: shareholder returns increase (SEK 4,560m of buybacks, 39.0m shares, 15.07m cancelled), balance-sheet utilisation increase (EUR 864m redeemed early, covenants amended, 40% of proceeds to debt), perimeter reduction (SEK 24,000m or about 18% of gross asset value), strategy change ("Back to Basics", 10% return on equity, 7.5% project hurdle), standards improvement (13 to 10 executives, 60 roles, bonuses cancelled), other actor changes (board and C-suite), and chief executive change (Ahlsén, ex-Akelius). Only guidance increase and sensible acquisitive step-up fail. That is a top-decile event cluster against a peer set where Carmila scores B and MERLIN Properties D.

Step two: the base the change acts on is not robust, which is why Element E1 nets to C rather than B. Four of five base tests fail. Absence of external headwinds grades F: hybrid work is settled, 57% of corporates plan to cut portfolio size, Stockholm central-business-district reversionary potential is minus 13%, three-year Swedish leases reprice fast, sub-letting and co-working handbacks add competing supply, and the Energy Performance of Buildings Directive is projected to triple Nordic renovation rates with Boverket transposing by 29 May 2026 at 214 kWh per square metre per year for offices. Delivery congruency grades D on four consecutive consensus misses (4.0%, 4.7%, 1.6%, 0.5% across Q2-25 to Q1-26) plus a Q1-26 revenue miss of SEK 96m or 4.0%. Mispricing grades D and low multiple grades C. Only "well-invested base" reaches C, and even there certification at 59% lags Fabege at 82% and Wihlborgs at 90%, while Kista at 23.0% vacancy is direct evidence that part of the base is not well invested.
counter_case: The memo carried the counter-case at full force at every Element, and one of the counters is genuinely strong.

The strongest single counter, from Element E8: the framework exists to find exactly this setup. An owner-operator with an aligned 25.4% holder is retiring stock below asset value while cutting costs, and the false-friend flags are simply the transition costs of a deliberate shrink-to-quality programme. The memo rejects it on arithmetic rather than on principle: disposals cut recurring earnings by roughly 10% while the buyback retires about 8% of the share count, so the accretion is close to a wash before any operating deterioration. That rejection depends on a single Jefferies estimate, which the memo flags.
triggers: Reassessment triggers. (1) Three consecutive quarters of net letting above SEK 50m excluding any single lease above SEK 50m of annual contract value; the Earnings Review sets a comparable bar of three consecutive quarters above plus SEK 50m with renegotiation uplifts consistently above plus 3.0% without material tenant-improvement concessions. (2) The EUR 1,000m hybrid refinanced without cutting recurring cash earnings by more than 5%. (3) Economic occupancy above 91%, from 87.5%. (4) Share price below roughly SEK 110, restoring a discount above 30% to net reinstatement value of SEK 159 to 164. (5) The Akelius 25.4% stake resolved.

Thematic invalidation triggers carried from the live thematics file: the United States 30-year yield sustained below 4.75%, or United States measured productivity above 2% annualised for two consecutive quarters, would weaken Thematic 4 and flip the paradigm read.

Risk triggers that would force a re-read fastest: any actual credit downgrade to sub-investment grade, named in the Risks report as the trigger to re-run the whole pre-mortem; and a credit default by another major Nordic landlord, with Heimstaden Bostad named, which the Risks report judges would trigger a systemic liquidity freeze.

Key questions carried to Early-Stage Assessment if the case reactivates. How much of the roughly 10% recurring-earnings dilution from disposals is genuinely offset by the buyback. What the remaining portfolio's stabilised vacancy actually is once the disposal mix effect is stripped out, since selling fully-let public-sector assets mechanically raises the vacancy of what remains. What the Kista 23.0% vacancy pocket is worth on a realistic exit yield, since the group's 5.62% average valuation yield cannot be the right mark for a bottom-decile sub-market. What the Entra ASA holding is actually worth to Castellum shareholders, given SEK 11.27bn of trapped equity, dual negative control with Balder at 39.98% and a failed mandatory offer.

Element-level downstream actions. Re-test the net reinstatement value discount at each quarterly print, since the gap moved 10 percentage points on price alone. Track income from property management per share against the SEK 9.36 FY25 base. Re-score Castellum against Thematic 4 when the Assistant Portfolio Manager runs the outstanding batch re-score, since the April-vintage Portfolio Impact Matrix carries no Thematic 4 column. Monitor the United States 30-year yield as the single best tracker of this stock's thematic risk. Track the problem count quarterly and re-test the simplicity guardrail once the hybrid is refinanced and the Akelius stake is resolved. Request reconciliation of the aggregate premium-to-book claim against the Skåne discount. Build the Early-Stage Assessment carve-out around Required Attribute RA3, tracking the nine deltas quarterly. Monitor the trough-on-trough supply leg, specifically Swedish construction starts and portfolio valuation yields. Track net letting excluding any single lease above SEK 50m of annual value. Test the Swedish interest-deduction reform's cash impact against the SEK 860m of non-deductible interest once enacted.

Setup carve-outs identified for later stages. Primary: Element E8 Required Attribute RA3, strong corporate-change-driven earnings upgrade or transformation, at A, where seven of nine deltas fire. Secondary: Element E8 Required Attribute RA6, trough-on-trough turn in a solid-quality cyclical, at D, where the supply leg is forming (construction starts collapsed, write-downs ceased, valuation yield flat at 5.62%, right-sizing executed) but the demand leg and the capitulation leg are both absent.
